project.formal_title: HalluciGuard-Eye: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Hallucination Detection and Mitigation in Ophthalmic Multimodal Large Language Models
project.domain: ophthalmic multimodal generation, hallucination detection, and clinical evidence grounding

framework.basis: The implementation details identify LLaVA-1.5, ViT-L/14, Vicuna-13B, AdamW, and mixed-precision training.

venue.basis: The PDF uses IEEE Access branding and layout, but its DOI, publication date, authors, and current-version fields are unresolved template text.

equations.claim: Candidate responses maximize weighted factuality minus a diversity penalty.
equations.note: Factuality reranking is implemented; the paper does not report a numerical diversity coefficient.

equations.claim: TransE uses margin ranking with L2 distance and corrupted head or tail entities.
ViT-L/14 produces visual tokens.
The text encoder produces response-segment tokens.
Visual-to-text scaled dot-product attention.
Text-to-visual scaled dot-product attention.
Matched image-text pairs use contrastive softmax loss with temperature 0.07.
Alignment score uses pooled directed contexts, their product, an MLP, and a sigmoid.
The CFGN query is the mean embedding of response entities.
Initial triplet retrieval accepts a head or tail cosine score above 0.75.
Subgraph expansion uses two hops and relation score threshold 0.6.
Grounding is the mean over claims of maximum evidence similarity.
Candidate score combines log probability, alignment, and grounding with weights 0.3 and 0.4.
The maximum-scoring candidate is selected.
Linearized knowledge evidence is encoded by a lightweight transformer.
Visual-to-text attention is mean pooled before fusion.
The fusion gate is a sigmoid over hidden, alignment, and evidence features.
The fused hidden state interpolates between decoder hidden state and fused context.
Anatomical accuracy is the mean of anatomical verification indicators.
Pathological characterization is a severity-weighted pathology similarity.
Recommendation validity is knowledge-graph support with path length at most three.
HFS is 0.25 AA plus 0.40 PC plus 0.35 CRV.
Stage 1 loss combines MLM, ITM, and KGE with weights 0.5 and 0.3.
Stage 2 combines generation, alignment, grounding, and HFS losses with weights 0.4, 0.3, and 0.3.
Stage 3 uses clinical reward and KL regularization with coefficient 0.1.
